text:
Recent work supports distinguishing elapsed time from interaction order, but this search found no direct 2023–2026 NextItNet extension establishing learned temporal resets. [TiCoSeRec (AAAI 2023)](https://ojs.aaai.org/index.php/AAAI/article/view/25540) associates irregular interaction gaps with preference drift and introduces interval-aware augmentation. [TALE (2024 preprint)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.07382) explicitly separates sequential order from timestamps through interval-aware weighting. [E-NSDE (NeurIPS 2024)](https://proceedings.neurips.cc/paper_files/paper/2024/hash/7cdbd53dfbcf9a5263227555aac5b9cd-Abstract-Conference.html) models continuous preference evolution and interval-dependent uncertainty. These motivate temporal features; they do not establish that every long gap makes older preferences irrelevant.

A compatible experimental hypothesis: retain [NextItNet’s dilated residual convolutions](https://arxiv.org/abs/1808.05163), but multiply each causal convolution tap by a jointly learned channel-wise decay, exp(−softplus(a)·log1p(elapsed_time)). Compute elapsed time between the receiving position and each historical tap using observed timestamps only. A learned soft boundary could instead attenuate taps crossing large gaps; this is a proposed adaptation, not a verified result from these papers. Mask padding before convolution and after residual updates, use normalization independently at each position, and read the final nonpadding position. Boundary masking must apply throughout the stack to prevent indirect information transfer across resets.

Controls: unchanged backbone; order-distance-only gates; real timestamp gates; shuffled gaps with item order preserved; fixed decay versus learned decay; soft attenuation versus hard resets. Compare matched capacity and training budgets, selecting by macro validation HR@10. Treat gaps as observable timing signals rather than observed intent or verified session boundaries. All gates remain internal to one jointly trained NextItNet per category; no separately fitted temporal scorer.
